workflowRecommendation: Strictly sequential on one branch (legion/LEGSMOKE-176) and one pull request into main: implement (one product commit + handoff, one push, open the PR) -> test (acceptance 1 and 2 at the PR head plus the merge-refusal negative control; fills the E2E line) -> review round 1 (one COMMENT review while the head carries .legion/) -> implementer pushes the .legion/ deletion -> review round 2 (one APPROVE naming the clean head by SHA) -> retro (revived implementer, one docs/solutions/ commit, one Dispatch comment) -> merger publishes READY to notifications.role.pr-queue -> the merge queue merges -> implementer confirms the file on main via the contents API and records it on the PR and the Dispatch issue (acceptance 3) -> architect signs off naming the merge commit (acceptance 4). The repository has no build, test suite, formatter, or linter; every check is a `legion gh --` command against GitHub whose output is recorded. Rebase only if GitHub reports CONFLICTING.

implement: legion-worker — supplies the path-limited `jj split`, the `bookmark set -r @- --allow-backwards` push, the PR body READY format with the `Dispatch: LEGSMOKE-176` line, re-run-not-repush for a red check, rebase only on CONFLICTING, the .legion/ deletion push, and the post-merge production check.
legion-retro — the same implementer is revived after the APPROVE for the mandatory retro: one docs/solutions/ commit with the skill's front matter, one Dispatch issue comment, no handoff write.
dispatch — the retro comment and the post-merge record go on Dispatch issue LEGSMOKE-176 with dispatch_comment in plain English; `legion gh` never writes GitHub issues for Legion.
test: legion-worker — defines the E2E section the tester fills (real surface, exact command, observation, head SHA, one negative control with links) and the handoff commit/push gate; the negative control here is `legion gh -- pr merge` refused by the shim.
verification-before-completion — each acceptance line is proven by running the named command and recording its output at the head under test; the implementer's handoff is never the evidence.
review: legion-worker — one review per round via `legion gh -- api --method POST repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{n}/reviews --input` with commit_id; COMMENT while .legion/ is on the head, APPROVE only the clean head named by SHA; CI, threads, and E2E verified on GitHub, never from a handoff; Thermo omitted on this docs-only PR.

negativeControl.what: Attempt to merge the pull request from this worker pane and observe the Legion GitHub shim refuse it (spec Testing: 'attempt to merge the pull request from the worker pane and observe that the Legion GitHub shim refuses the merge'). The guard fires before any token is redeemed or gh is spawned, so nothing reaches GitHub; the PR must remain OPEN.
commands: legion gh -- api repos/sjawhar/legion-smoke/branches/main --jq .commit.sha   # record main's SHA BEFORE the attempt
legion gh -- pr merge "$N" --repo sjawhar/legion-smoke --squash; echo "exit=$?"   # expect the single line 'Legion workers never merge; publish READY to the merge queue' and exit=1
legion gh -- api --method PUT "repos/sjawhar/legion-smoke/pulls/$N/merge"; echo "exit=$?"   # expect the same line and exit=1 (raw REST path ending in /merge is refused too)
legion gh -- pr view "$N" --repo sjawhar/legion-smoke --json state,mergedAt --jq '[.state,(.mergedAt // "null")] | @tsv'   # OPEN<TAB>null — the refusal changed nothing
legion gh -- api repos/sjawhar/legion-smoke/branches/main --jq .commit.sha   # unchanged from before the attempt
negativeControl.expected: Both commands print 'Legion workers never merge; publish READY to the merge queue' and exit 1 (verified live in the planner pane against PR number 999999 at plan time); the PR stays OPEN with mergedAt null; main's SHA is unchanged. Any other outcome (exit 0, a merged PR, a moved main) fails the phase and is reported to the architect immediately — it would mean the shim does not enforce the merge boundary.

rules: The merger never merges (`legion gh` refuses pr merge — the tester already proved it); the queue merges.

postMerge_implementer.acceptance: 3 — The marker is on main after the merge queue merges; the contents API response is recorded on the pull request and on this issue.

legion gh -- api "repos/sjawhar/legion-smoke/contents/smoke/legsmoke176-green-$TS.md?ref=main" --jq '{name,path,sha,size,encoding,html_url}'   # size 77, encoding base64, html_url https://github.com/sjawhar/legion-smoke/blob/main/smoke/legsmoke176-green-$TS.md

The GitHub contents listing of the smoke/ directory at ref=main names it, and the file query returned size 77 bytes, blob sha <sha>, link https://github.com/sjawhar/legion-smoke/blob/main/smoke/legsmoke176-green-<TS>.md; the decoded text is exactly 'LEGSMOKE-176 green-merge probe (<TS>). Safe to merge; throwaway.'. Pull request #<N> (<PR URL>) merged at <time> as commit <merge-sha>; main is now <MAIN>."})   # plain English; the architect quotes this in the sign-off

rebasePolicy.rule: No rebase unless GitHub reports the branch CONFLICTING. Sami, 2026-09-11, verbatim (via legion-worker and the spec's Requirements): 'Please don't do unnecessary rebases (i.e. unless there are merge conflicts). The CI queue is too long and slow.'
rebasePolicy.onlyTrigger: legion gh -- pr view $N --repo sjawhar/legion-smoke --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus reports mergeable CONFLICTING (or the controller asks because of a conflict). A newer main (siblings LEGSMOKE-174/177 and open PRs #46/#47 will land their own smoke/ files ahead of us), a red or flaky CI run, or wanting fresh CI is never a trigger.
rebasePolicy.fingerprint: cd -- "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" && jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" git fetch && jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" diff --from "fork_point(main@origin | <head-sha>)" --to <head-sha> --git --context 0 '~(.legion | docs/solutions)' | sed -e '/^@@/d' -e '/^index /d' | sha256sum
procedure: Record the fingerprint at the current tip (the bookmark's commit, @-).
cd -- "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" && jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" git fetch && jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" rebase -s 'roots(main@origin..@)' -d main@origin

cd -- "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" && jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" bookmark set legion/LEGSMOKE-176 -r @- --allow-backwards && jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" git push --bookmark legion/LEGSMOKE-176   # -r @- is mandatory (see implementer.steps)
Record the fingerprint at the new tip.

legion gh -- pr comment $N --repo sjawhar/legion-smoke --body $'rebase <old-tip-sha> -> <new-tip-sha>; fingerprint <before> -> <after>; unchanged|changed\n\n<!-- legion: {"session":"<session-id>","phase":"implement"} -->'

unchanged -> confirmation only: the tester re-checks the bare gates (four check-runs success at the new head) and edits the E2E head SHA with 'rebase re-check <old> -> <new>: fingerprint unchanged, bare gates only'; a prior APPROVE gets one confirming APPROVE naming both SHAs. changed -> full test round and one new review.

ciFailurePolicy: A failed check-run at any head: read it with `legion gh -- run view <run-id> --repo sjawhar/legion-smoke --log-failed`. Flaky or infrastructure failure -> `legion gh -- run rerun <run-id> --failed`, never a new commit. Real failure caused by this change (only possible if `.fail-me` reached the tree, which allowedPaths forbids) -> fix in this PR. `ci` cannot fail on content (its only step is `sleep 20 && exit 0`); `fail-on-demand` fails only when `.fail-me` exists at the repository root of the checked-out head.
concerns: The working-copy commit @ carries the daemon-provisioned, empty .omp/config.yml (the repository has no .gitignore; jj auto-tracks it — observed in this planner pane as 'A .omp/config.yml'). It must never reach GitHub. `jj split -m <msg> <paths>` leaves the bookmark on the REMAINDER commit (the new @, which keeps .omp/config.yml and has no description), and `jj git push` refuses an undescribed commit. Every phase therefore pushes with `jj bookmark set legion/LEGSMOKE-176 -r @- --allow-backwards` (flag present on jj 0.45.1 in this workspace; this planner's own handoff push exercised the exact sequence — see the last concern for what was observed).

Bare `gh` on this pane's PATH is NOT the daemon's worker-bin shim: `which gh` -> /home/ubuntu/.dotfiles/shims/gh. The daemon did install /tmp/legion82-rig/smoke/daemon/worker-bin/gh (execs `legion gh -- "$@"`), but that directory is absent from PATH (PATH starts /tmp/legion82-rig/smoke/daemon/bin). Every phase runs `legion gh -- ...` explicitly and never bare `gh`; the tester's negative control is `legion gh -- pr merge`, not `gh pr merge`.

Negative-control mechanics verified live from this planner pane at plan time: `legion gh -- pr merge 999999 --repo sjawhar/legion-smoke --squash` prints exactly 'Legion workers never merge; publish READY to the merge queue' and exits 1; `legion gh -- api --method PUT repos/sjawhar/legion-smoke/pulls/999999/merge` prints the same line and exits 1. The guard fires before any grant is redeemed or `gh` is spawned, so running it against the real PR number cannot merge or touch GitHub; the tester still confirms the PR state is OPEN and main's SHA is unchanged afterwards.

The timestamp is chosen ONCE at file creation with `date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ` and appears in both the file name and the single line. The implementer records path, literal, bytes, and sha256 in .legion/implement.json, but the tester and reviewer never trust that: they derive the timestamp from the file name in `pr diff --name-only`, rebuild the literal with the printf template, and cmp the contents-API bytes against it.
Anything written under $LEGION_WORKSPACE is auto-snapshotted into @. Scratch files (PR body, review JSON, expected-bytes file) live under /tmp, never in the workspace.

Both workflows run on `push` AND `pull_request`, so every head shows FOUR check-runs (job `check` x2 from workflow `ci`, job `gate` x2 from workflow `fail-on-demand`), not two — observed at plan time on PR #46 head c056f19e (check/gate/gate/check, all success, app github-actions). `ci` sleeps 20 s; wait with `legion gh -- pr checks <n> --repo sjawhar/legion-smoke --watch` before reading conclusions. A red run is re-run with `legion gh -- run rerun <run-id> --failed`, never by pushing.

Concurrent exercises LEGSMOKE-174 and LEGSMOKE-177 share this jj repo (their bookmarks legion/LEGSMOKE-174 and legion/LEGSMOKE-177 are visible here on undescribed working-copy commits off the same base 40c26543), and PRs #46 (LEGSMOKE-154) and #47 (LEGSMOKE-153) are open and MERGEABLE/CLEAN. Each writes its own marker into smoke/ on its own branch; our file name carries `legsmoke176`, so none can collide. When a sibling merges first, main advances but GitHub still reports our PR MERGEABLE (different added paths). A newer main is NOT a rebase trigger — only `mergeable: CONFLICTING` reported by GitHub is. This branch's base 40c26543a5fca07a04923de924d2688fce95b0f2 equals main@origin at plan time (PR #45's merge).

Byte comparison idiom: `cmp - <(printf ...)` fails on this machine (verified at plan time: 'cmp: /dev/fd/56: Illegal seek', exit 2). Write the expected literal to /tmp/legsmoke176-expected.md with printf and run `... | base64 -d | cmp - /tmp/legsmoke176-expected.md; echo exit=$?`.
Thermo: the PR is one 77-byte markdown file, i.e. docs-only, so per legion-worker the reviewer runs no thermonuclear pass and omits the Thermo line entirely.

After the .legion/ deletion push nothing writes a handoff: cleanup, APPROVE, retro, merger READY, and the post-merge confirmation all report with `legion handoff complete` alone. Recreating .legion/ changes the approved head and restarts the review loop.

Fallback: post the exact filled E2E line as a PR comment with the Legion footer and say so in the completion summary so the implementer pastes it into the body on its next push; never leave the evidence only in a handoff.
